notes.musome: A command to a group: mu- … -e.

guidebook.intro: School vocabulary is full of commands. Teachers speak to the whole class, so you’ll hear plural commands all day.

tips.title: Commands to a group
body: To one person, a command is the bare verb: **Soma** (read), **Wandiika** (write). To a group, add **mu-** in front and change the final **-a** to **-e**: **Musome**, **Muwandiike**, **Muwulirize**.
The same **-e** ending makes “let’s”: **Tusome** (let’s read). You’ll meet it again in **Tugende** (let’s go).

tips.title: n- changes the sound after it
body: When **n-** (I) meets **w**, it becomes **mp**: **wandiika** gives **mpandiika** (I write). With **l** or **r** it becomes **nd**: **laba** gives **ndaba** (I see). You have seen this in **mpulira** and **mpa** too.

culture.title: Languages at school
body: Uganda has over forty languages. Schools teach in English, and many in central Uganda also teach Luganda. It is common to grow up speaking three languages.
